objective.statement: Write and recognise the scales of B♭ major and E♭ major.
successCriteria: I know B♭ major has two flats: B♭ and E♭.
I know E♭ major has three flats: B♭, E♭ and A♭.

explanation.text: Some major scales use flats instead of sharps. F major (from Grade 1) has one flat. B♭ major has two, and E♭ major has three.

music.textAlternative: The scale of B flat major going up: B flat, C, D, E flat, F, G, A, B flat.

explanation.caption: B♭ major: B♭ C D E♭ F G A B♭. The flats are B♭ and E♭.

music.textAlternative: The scale of E flat major going up: E flat, F, G, A flat, B flat, C, D, E flat.

explanation.caption: E♭ major: E♭ F G A♭ B♭ C D E♭. The flats are B♭, E♭ and A♭.

explanation.text: The pattern is still tone, tone, semitone, tone, tone, tone, semitone. In B♭ major the semitones are D to E♭ and A to B♭.
Again each letter appears once: it is E♭ and not D♯ in the scale of B♭.
Flat keys so far: F (1 flat), B♭ (2 flats), E♭ (3 flats). Flats are added in the order B, E, A.

music.textAlternative: The scale of E flat major going up with three flats.

steps: Start on E♭. Play E♭, F, G: two tones.
G to A♭ is the first semitone. Then A♭ to B♭, B♭ to C and C to D are tones.
D to E♭ is the last semitone.
demonstration.textAlternative: The scale of E flat major in the treble clef: E flat, F, G, A flat, B flat, C, D, E flat.
